subject: panel model including interaction between predictors

messages.subject: panel model including interaction between predictors
parts:
Hi everyone, 

I'm attempting to run a dynamic panel model with 4 waves of data. The original model is adapted from the Allison model ( https://doi.org/10.1177/2378023117710578 ) but I would like to add a second predictor and the interaction term of the two predictors to the model.

Generally, the idea is as follows:
Symptoms (scl) are predicted by alliance (wai) and agency (tai), as well as the interaction between alliance and agency (tai_wai).

I've included the interaction term as a product variable (as one would do in regression), but I'm not sure if this is the right way to do it. 
I can run the model, but lavaan gives me a warning message (In lav_model_hessian(lavmodel = lavmodel, lavsamplestats = lavsamplestats,  :
  lavaan WARNING: Hessian is not fully symmetric. Max diff = 3.03223187358981e-06). Is this likely due to model misspecification or an issue with my data?

Any ideas would be greatly appreciated!

(Here's my model code:)

model.3 <- '
# define random intercept to control for between person differences in scl (except scl.1)
scl.between =~ 1*scl5 + 1*scl10 + 1*scl15 +1*scl20 
scl.between ~~ scl1

# define autoregressive and lagged effects on scl, assuming statiority of covariances
scl5 ~ auto*scl1 + lagged1*tai1 + lagged2*wai1 + lagged3*tai_wai1
scl10 ~ auto*scl5 + lagged1*tai5 + lagged2*wai5 + lagged3*tai_wai5
scl15 ~ auto*scl10 + lagged1*tai10 + lagged2*wai10 + lagged3*tai_wai10
scl20 ~ auto*scl15 + lagged1*tai15 + lagged2*wai15 + lagged3*tai_wai15

# allow for correlations of between-person differences in scl and tai and wai and the interaction term
scl.between ~~ tai1
scl.between ~~ wai1
scl.between ~~ tai_wai1
scl.between ~~ tai5
scl.between ~~ wai5
scl.between ~~ tai_wai5
scl.between ~~ tai10
scl.between ~~ wai10
scl.between ~~ tai_wai10
scl.between ~~ tai15
scl.between ~~ wai15
scl.between ~~ tai_wai15

# allow for associations between (residualized, i.e. person-centered) scl and tai (& wai & the interaction) at the same time-point
scl1 ~~ tai1
scl1 ~~ wai1
scl1 ~~ tai_wai1
scl5 ~~ tai5
scl5 ~~ wai5
scl5 ~~ tai_wai5
scl10 ~~ tai10
scl10 ~~ wai10
scl10 ~~ tai_wai10
scl15 ~~ tai15
scl15 ~~ wai15
scl15 ~~ tai_wai15

# assumes homoscedastic residual variances in scl across measurement occasions (i.e., stationarity of variances)
scl5 ~~ scl.within*scl5
scl10 ~~ scl.within*scl10
scl15 ~~ scl.within*scl15
scl20 ~~ scl.within*scl20

# allows for correlations of tai ( & wai & the interaction term) across measurement occasions
tai1 ~~ wai1; tai1 ~~ tai_wai1; 
tai1 ~~ tai5; tai1 ~~ wai5; tai1 ~~ tai_wai5;
tai1 ~~ tai10; tai1 ~~ wai10; tai1 ~~ tai_wai10;
tai1 ~~ tai15; tai1 ~~ wai15; tai1 ~~ tai_wai15;
tai5 ~~ wai5; tai5 ~~ tai_wai5;
tai5 ~~ tai10; tai5 ~~ wai10; tai5 ~~ tai_wai10;
tai5 ~~ tai15; tai5 ~~ wai15; tai5 ~~ tai_wai15;
tai10 ~~ wai10; tai10 ~~ tai_wai10;
tai10 ~~ tai15; tai10 ~~ wai15; tai10 ~~ tai_wai15;
tai15 ~~ wai15; tai15 ~~ tai_wai15;


wai1 ~~ tai_wai1;
wai1 ~~ tai5; wai1 ~~ wai5; wai1 ~~ tai_wai5;
wai1 ~~ tai10; wai1 ~~ wai10; wai1 ~~ tai_wai10;
wai1 ~~ tai15; wai1 ~~ wai15; wai1 ~~ tai_wai15;
wai5 ~~ tai_wai5;
wai5 ~~ tai10; wai5 ~~ wai10; wai5 ~~ tai_wai10;
wai5 ~~ tai15; wai5 ~~ wai15; wai5 ~~ tai_wai15;
wai10 ~~ tai_wai10;
wai10 ~~ tai15; wai10 ~~ wai15; wai10 ~~ tai_wai15;
wai15 ~~ tai_wai15;

tai_wai1 ~~ tai5; tai_wai1 ~~ wai5; tai_wai1 ~~ tai_wai5; 
tai_wai1 ~~ tai10; tai_wai1 ~~ wai10; tai_wai1 ~~ tai_wai10;
tai_wai1 ~~ tai15; tai_wai1 ~~ wai15; tai_wai1 ~~ tai_wai15;
tai_wai5 ~~ tai10; tai_wai5 ~~ wai10; tai_wai5 ~~ tai_wai10; 
tai_wai5 ~~ tai15; tai_wai5 ~~ wai15; tai_wai5 ~~ tai_wai15;
tai_wai10 ~~ tai15; tai_wai10 ~~ wai15; tai_wai10 ~~ tai_wai15
'

Simone

I am not familiar with this type of model, but here a few comments based on the SAS syntax of the paper.
In the paper there are no covariances between alpha/scl.between and the predictors, but you do have those covariances. I see those covariances in the model presented in figure 1 but i dont see them in the syntax. And the syntax specifically states a covariances between alpha ~~ ed equal to 0.

Thats the main difference I see from your syntax and the SAS syntax from the paper, I might still be missing something else
